integrity: The universal estimate is reconstructed from the boundary Fourier decomposition of a bounded harmonic map and the classical endpoint Riesz projection L-infinity to BMO theorem, followed by the standard BMOA Carleson characterization. Sharpness uses the full primary 2026 construction for every distortion parameter and the elementary implication that bounded f plus bounded g would force h bounded. The primary source date and MSC classification were checked directly.
scientific_limitations: The theorem identifies BMOA as a universal quantitative endpoint and proves failure of the stronger H-infinity target on every fixed globally univalent K-quasiconformal class with K>1. It does not claim an optimal numerical BMOA constant, minimality among all intermediate function spaces, or a classification of extra geometric hypotheses that restore bounded components.
title: BMOA is the sharp endpoint for bounded harmonic splitting
